messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT PAGER — streaming p99 latency breach detected for prod-region-us-east-1. Alert group: inference-streaming-p99. Root cause suspected: accelerated node degradation. Pager: oncall-sre

incident-bot: summary: p99 spiked to 3.2s (baseline ~180ms), p95 ~850ms, elevated streaming stalls and client disconnects. Affected pool: gpu-pool-az3 (models: rdx-large-v2 streaming). Auto-failover attempts: 2 (partial)

sara (oncall): I'm on it. pulling up grafana now — can someone post the node list for gpu-pool-az3 and recent alerts from node exporter?

ben (eng-sre): checking. I see node gpu-node-az3-17 with rising ECC correctable error counts since ~10:12UTC and NVML reports thermal events at 10:18UTC. Metrics: correctable_errors rate went 0 -> 120/min. Also kernel OOPS style chatter in dmesg around 10:19.

li (eng-runtime): that matches streaming tail we saw. KV cache lookups timed out when a bucket was pinned to that node. Routing tried fallback but some sessions are pinned and stalled. ramp-up of p99 coincides with a sudden drop in concurrent workers on gpu-node-az3-17.

ben (eng-sre): grabbing logs from the node. attaching small snippets — removing sensitive tokens.

ben (eng-sre): ```
# dmesg | tail -n 40
[10:17:55] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): Correctable ECC error detected, vendor: 0x10de
[10:18:11] thermal: GPU0: reached temp limit, throttling
[10:18:12] GPU watchdog: stall detected, preemption delayed
[10:18:15] GPU0: reset requested
[10:18:17] nvidia-mig: mig instance lost
```

ben (eng-sre): ```
# nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,THERMAL
GPU 0:
  ECC errors (correctable): 152
  Temperature: 92 C
  Power: 250W (throttling)
```

sara (oncall): 92C is high. sounds like thermal throttle + ECC noise -> flaky behavior. We should drain traffic off that node ASAP and trigger a graceful eviction of sessions. Li, can runtime re-route new streams away and allow existing to failover?

li (eng-runtime): yes. Plan: 1) mark node unschedulable in kube. 2) trigger session handoff for in-flight streaming via our takeover path (fast-failover). 3) temporarily increase pool fallback weight to spare nodes. I'll run commands with Ben.

manny (eng-platform): I'll prepare a spare node in the same AZ (gpu-node-az3-spare-2) and bump pool replicas by +2 as backup. Also prepping autoscaler to prefer non-throttled zones for new allocs.

ben (eng-sre): executing cordon + drain now. Running: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-az3-17 && kubectl drain gpu-node-az3-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=30`

ben (eng-sre): drain started. Noting some long-lived streams are refusing to migrate (clients with pinned connections). We'll request a soft restart for the runtime agent on that node to trigger session handoff hooks.

li (eng-runtime): doing `kubectl exec -n runtime-agent runtime-agent-az3-17 -- /usr/bin/runtimectl handoff --force` on agent side. Also bumping fallback weight: `redwoodctl routing update --pool gpu-pool-az3 --fallback-weight 0.75` (quick temporary change).

aleks (customer-success): seeing multiple customer tickets flagged with streaming stalls and slow responses. I'm drafting an outbound note: short impact summary (partial degradation for US-East streaming at 10:12–10:40UTC), mitigation steps we are taking, and ETA for full restoration TBD. Will update once nodes stabilized.

ben (eng-sre): drain finished. Pod evacuations: 87/90 migrated. 3 sessions required forced kill to allow failover. Post-drain nvml shows GPU resets.

ben (eng-sre): post-evac check: ```
# nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,THERMAL
GPU 0:
  ECC errors (correctable): 7 (post-reset, last 5m)
  Temperature: 48 C
```

li (eng-runtime): routing change propagated. p99 dropped to 480ms within 60s of routing change; p95 back to ~210ms. some residual tail for sessions that were killed — we'll track those user-level errors.

sara (oncall): good mitigation. Next: isolate node for hardware triage. Ben — can you tag gpu-node-az3-17 for hardware inspection and schedule a replacement? record: serial SN=GX-AV-412.

ben (eng-sre): tagged and out-of-rotation. Filing hw ticket: HWT-2026-198 with vendor. Recommend replacing card; we'll also run extended memtest and ECC scrub. Keeping node offline until cleared.

manny (eng-platform): spare node joined pool and autoscaler bump applied. I'm monitoring cost/scale hit. Also enabling a temporary policy to avoid single-node session pins: `routing.policy.session_affinity = zone_prefer` for 30m.

aleks (customer-success): sending update to affected customers: apologizing for disruption, note that we routed around faulty hardware and restored normal p95/p99 for new sessions. offering an incident follow-up once PMs have postmortem. :email:

sara (oncall): action items: 1) Ben to run memtest and update hw ticket. 2) Li to validate runtime handoff hooks and add metrics to detect early ECC escalation. 3) Manny to review autoscaler pref rules to avoid concentrated sessions. 4) I'll own initial incident timeline for postmortem.

ben (eng-sre): noted. memtest scheduled and I'll attach logs. vendor intake scheduled for tomorrow.

li (eng-runtime): will add an alert rule: if ECC correctable rate > 50/min AND thermal > 85C => preemptively shift hot-buckets off node. Will open a PR for the alert and add a gating runbook.

sara (oncall): great. closing the pager loop for now — p99 stable, pool healthy. leaving thread open for postmortem items. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — Mitigation complete, severity reduced to SEV-2 (monitoring). Refer to ticket HWT-2026-198 for hardware replacement and to INC-3498765432 for postmortem assignment.
